title: Capacity Conductor: Console Lattice for Fleet Scaling, Throughput Views, and Change Chronicle
creator: Priya Shah
description: Build a cohesive Console surface (Capacity Conductor: 'Lattice') that unifies per-fleet scaling controls, live and historical throughput visualizations, and an immutable change chronicle for autoscale/override events. The goal is to give operators a single place to tune throughput guarantees, inspect scaling behavior, and audit who changed what and when without jumping between multiple dashboards.
background: Customers with Dedicated capacity told us they struggle to reconcile why fleets scaled unexpectedly and who applied overrides. Current Console surfaces are fragmented: scaling toggles in one pane, throughput charts in another, and audit log exports in a separate admin view. This causes slow ops during incidents and drives support tickets asking for better traceability and safer rollback UX.
acceptance_criteria: A single Capacity Conductor panel available from Fleet detail that exposes scaling controls, current throughput SLOs, and a timeline of scaling events
Operators can set and preview autoscaling policies (min/max vGPU, target qps, warm pools) and save as named policy templates
Throughput dashboard shows live p50/p95 latency, token/s throughput, and request distribution by route and model for the selected fleet over selectable windows (1m, 15m, 1h, 24h)
Change Chronicle records: actor, timestamp, diff of policy, reason/note, and linked GitHub PR or support ticket ID; entries are immutable and exportable as CSV
A rollback action is available for the last committed policy with an explainable impact estimate (expected capacity change and cost delta)
All new telemetry and events are instrumented and available to the Console backplane and to metrics dashboards (Prometheus/Grafana) for alerts
tasks: PM: Finalize field-level schema for autoscale policy and change record
Design: Mock capacity conductor panel for desktop and tablet; include quick-actions and rollback modal
Design: Define color/visual cadence for throughput bands (normal, degraded, saturated)
Eng: Implement policy API endpoints (GET/PUT/POST audits) and change-channels stream
Eng: Wire frontend to streaming throughput feed and historical query service
Eng: Persist immutable change records with actor metadata and optional ticket link
QA: Simulate scaling events and verify rollback flow and export correctness
Docs: Write Console help doc and runbook for operators
engineering_notes: Prefer incremental rollout behind feature flag 'capacity-conductor-lattice' scoped to beta accounts
API contract: POST /fleets/:id/policies (body: policy_name, min_gpus, max_gpus, target_rps, warm_pool_pct, cooldown_s, note)
Telemetry events: policy.create, policy.update, policy.rollback, scaling.event (include estimated_cost_delta, pre_state, post_state)
Backend: store change chronicle in append-only table with strong consistency; consider event-sourcing to keep auditability
Frontend: stream throughput via websocket aggregation service to avoid polling costs at high fleet counts
rollout_plan: Alpha: Internal only behind flag (2 weeks) - validate schema, telemetry, and basic UI
Beta: Invite 5 customers with dedicated fleets (3 weeks) - monitor scaling correctness and operator feedback
GA: Gradual enablement to all Dedicated customers with migration guide and default audit retention (90 days)
qa_checks: Verify policy validation prevents contradictory min>max entries
Simulate burst traffic and confirm autoscaler respects warm_pool_pct and cooldown_s
Confirm Change Chronicle entries include actor and linked ticket if provided
Test rollback: ensure that reverting to prior policy restores previous scaling behavior within expected cooldown
Export CSV and cross-check with raw audit store for fidelity
notes: This initiative should reduce high-severity support incidents caused by unexpected autoscaling changes and improve operator confidence for making proactive capacity adjustments.
